# Screw-cutting lathe with slide rest (`lathe_screw_cutting`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/manufacturing.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Tools, machines & manufacturing (`manufacturing`)
- Deps: needs screw_nut_bolt, gears_gear_trains; helped by crank_connecting_rod, belt_drive, crucible_steel, blast_furnace_cast_iron
- Core idea: On a lathe the work turns and the tool is held against it. On the old pole lathe the turner holds the tool by hand; accuracy depends on his skill. The industrial lathe has three things. An all-iron bed with straight guideways. A slide rest: a carriage that clamps the tool and moves it along and across by screws, so the cut is governed by the machine. And a long, accurate lead screw geared to the spindle through exchangeable wheels, which moves the carriage a fixed distance for every turn of the work. With that the lathe cuts true cylinders and screw threads of any pitch, copies the accuracy of its own lead screw, and can make a better lead screw for the next lathe. A first good screw is made by correcting a hand-cut one, using a long nut that averages its errors.
- Pitfalls:
  - A wooden bed or frame; it flexes and the work comes out tapered
  - Trying to cut threads freehand with a chasing tool for precision work
  - Play (backlash) in the screws: always approach the cut from the same side
  - Saying Maudslay invented the slide rest or the screw-cutting lathe; he combined known elements into the standard machine
- History: egypt: c. 300 BC – earliest picture of a lathe, tomb of Petosiris; turned objects are older in the eastern Mediterranean; china: lathe-turned work from the Warring States and Han periods; no screw-cutting; europe: 13th c. – pole lathe pictured; c. 1480 Mittelalterliches Hausbuch shows a screw-cutting lathe with a cross slide; 1569–1578 Jacques Besson; c. 1751–1760 Vaucanson's iron slide-rest lathe; 1770s Ramsden's screw-cutting lathes for instrument screws; 1795 Senot; c. 1797–1800 Henry Maudslay's all-metal lathe with slide rest, lead screw and change gears; americas: 1798 – David Wilkinson's slide-rest lathe patent, Rhode Island
- Read:
  - Robert S. Woodbury, History of the Lathe to 1850 (1961)
  - L. T. C. Rolt, Tools for the Job: A Short History of Machine Tools (1965)
